headline: All seven majors sit below their 200-day lines while BTC moves onto exchanges and ETF outflows persist
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it answers the only question that matters before you look at anything else: none of the seven assets in today's set, BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, BNB, DOGE, or ADA, are above their 200-day moving average. That is a full sweep. When one coin is below its 200-day it might be a local wound. When all seven are below it, you are looking at a market-wide trend, not a coin problem. BTC itself sits 49.0% off its 12-month high of $124,773.51, and the smaller-cap names are worse: ADA is 83.2% off its high, DOGE 75.7% off, SOL 70.4% off. Distance from highs like that tells you how much ground would need to be reclaimed before anyone could even argue the downtrend is over.

Momentum is where it gets more interesting, because it does not simply confirm the trend. BTC's RSI-14 sits at 47.4, dead center, neither overbought nor oversold, with MACD below signal. ETH's RSI is 56.3, the highest of the group, and its 7-day and 30-day changes are actually positive (+1.81% and +6.36%) even while it remains 60.6% below its own high and below its 200-day. That is a real divergence worth naming: ETH is showing short-term relative strength inside a market that is structurally still in a downtrend. BNB and DOGE show MACD above signal, a bullish crossover in the momentum indicator, while both remain below their 200-day lines and negative on RSI's oversold side (DOGE at 40.7). Momentum flickering positive under a still-bearish trend structure is the market resting or turning, not confirming.

Positioning adds texture rather than resolving it. BTC funding on OKX is running at 8.7% annualized, positive, meaning longs are paying shorts to hold their bets, an unusual position to be crowded into given price is down 0.34% on the day and 2.97% over 30 days. The long/short account ratio of 2.28 says more accounts are positioned long than short. Liquidations over the past 22 hours lean hard toward longs getting flushed: $6.12M in long liquidations against $1.59M in shorts. DOGE's funding is even richer at 11.0% annualized with a long/short ratio of 5.45, a genuinely crowded long book. SOL is the outlier with negative funding (-7.1% annualized), meaning shorts are paying longs there, a cheaper, less lopsided setup by comparison. Crowded and expensive (BTC, DOGE) is a more fragile perch than flat or short-funded (SOL).

Flows tell a story that argues with the funding data. Whale wallets moved a net $262.8 million onto exchanges over the past 72 hours, mostly BTC: $127.5M went to Coinbase Institutional and $117.4M to Binance, both classic deposit patterns that traders watch as a precursor to potential selling. The weekly trend behind that move has been choppy, not one-directional: the last four weekly readings were +$244.8M, +$1.06B, +$315.7M, and -$342.2M off-exchange, so today's onto-exchange move is a shift within a noisy series, not a clean continuation. On the ETF side, BTC spot funds saw -$131.1M net on 13 Aug 2026, extending to -$227.3M over the last five sessions, with same_direction_days at 2, too short a streak to call it anything more than a soft outflow stretch. ETH ETFs moved the opposite way: +$5.9M on the same day and +$46.6M over five sessions, a genuine split in traditional-finance appetite between the two largest assets. Stablecoin float, the market's dry powder, is essentially flat, down just 0.69% over 30 days to $306.3B, so this is not a story of capital fleeing crypto broadly.

Sentiment sits at 29, Fear, near the bottom of its own 30-day range of 25 to 33. That lines up with the exchange inflows and the ETF outflow stretch, for once the crowd's mood and the tape's flows are not contradicting each other. What would change the picture: a BTC funding flip to negative alongside the long/short ratio cooling off would signal the crowded long book unwinding rather than growing; a reclaim of the 200-day on any major, especially ETH given its current relative strength in RSI and 30-day returns, would break the seven-for-seven bearish sweep; and a shift in the ETF five-session net back toward inflow, with same_direction_days actually building in that direction, would mark a real change in the traditional-finance bid rather than a one-day print.
